docRequirement: memory.md:398 binds every agent write of a memory file: "When Claude writes a memory file that begins with YAML frontmatter, Claude Code records the write time in a `modified` frontmatter field as an ISO 8601 timestamp." Read whole, the line adds the scope and the ceiling: "Any file that has frontmatter gets the field the next time Claude writes it, including files created on earlier versions; Claude Code never adds frontmatter to a file that has none. The `modified` field requires Claude Code v2.1.214 or later." So the contract is exactly: on write, if the file's first line opens a `---` frontmatter block, set/refresh a `modified` key inside that block to an ISO-8601 timestamp; never synthesize frontmatter for a file that lacks it. The field is per-file (not per-entry), and its stated purpose is a freshness signal "both to you and to Claude when it reads the memory back".
divergence: The whole mechanism is absent: no writer inspects the first line for `---`, and no key named `modified` is ever emitted, so a memory file that DOES begin with frontmatter is appended to and left with a stale (or missing) timestamp forever. This is not a wrong key name for a right value: Nessy's nearest artefact, `<!-- nessy:auto:YYYY-MM-DD -->`, differs on all four axes the doc fixes -- location (trailing HTML comment on the bullet, not a frontmatter key), granularity (one date per entry, not one timestamp per file), precision (calendar day, not ISO-8601 instant) and audience (stripped at load, so the model never sees it, versus a value the doc puts in front of both user and model). Renaming it would satisfy nothing. Conversely the doc's negative half is already satisfied by accident, not by design: because both writers seed a new file as `# Memory\n\n- ...`, Nessy never adds frontmatter to a file that has none -- so the observable gap is confined to files whose frontmatter a human hand-authored. One second-order divergence rides along and constrains the fix: Claude Code strips frontmatter before loading the index (`memory.md:388`, min-version 2.1.211), while `readMemoryFile` (`memory-store.ts:29-33`) reads the raw first 200 lines, so in this fork a frontmatter block -- and any `modified:` line we add -- becomes prompt content inside the `<memory>` block rather than metadata.

change.what: New pure helper `export function stampMemoryModified(content: string, now: Date = new Date()): string`. Contract: strip a leading BOM for the first-line test only (mirror `parseRuleFile`'s `raw.replace(/^\uFEFF/, '')`, memory-store.ts:215); return `content` UNCHANGED unless line 0 trimmed === '---' AND some later line trimmed === '---' (the same open/close test parseRuleFile uses at memory-store.ts:217-219 -- an unclosed `---` is not frontmatter and must be left alone). Inside the block, replace the first line matching /^\s*modified\s*:/ with `modified: ${now.toISOString()}`; if no such line exists, insert that line immediately before the closing `---`. Do line-level surgery, NOT gray-matter's `matter.stringify` -- gray-matter is already a dependency here (packages/session-tools-core/package.json) but re-serialising reorders keys and requotes values in a file the user hand-wrote. Preserve the file's existing newline convention: detect '\r\n' and rejoin with it (memory-cleanup.ts:125 shows the repo's existing CRLF bail-out; do not inherit that limitation on the write path, or a CRLF MEMORY.md silently never gets stamped). Export it from packages/session-tools-core/src/index.ts.

Two lines, in this order so the no-op guard keeps its meaning: `const formatted = formatMemoryFile(existing, memory); if (formatted === existing) return; const next = stampMemoryModified(formatted);` then write `next` as today. Stamping BEFORE the equality check would make an empty/whitespace `memory` argument (which `formatMemoryFile` deliberately returns unchanged at :31) rewrite the file with a fresh timestamp for no recorded fact.

Same two-step as above around the local `formatMemoryFile` (:112-120), importing `stampMemoryModified` from '@nessy-agent/session-tools-core'. The dependency direction already allows this: packages/shared/package.json lists `@nessy-agent/session-tools-core: workspace:*` and shared already imports from it (e.g. agent/mode-manager.ts:25). Do NOT re-implement the helper here -- the marker constant is already duplicated across these two packages behind a 'keep in sync' comment (memory-store.ts:152-159 and remember.ts:14-21) and that is the drift this fix should not double.

Leave unstamped and record why in the existing comment block: the sweep is deterministic housekeeping, not an agent write, and the doc scopes the field to 'when Claude writes a memory file' whose purpose is 'how current the fact is'. Stamping it would advance the timestamp on a day when no fact changed. Write the decision down rather than leaving it as an unexplained omission.

blastRadius: Writers touched: the `remember` session tool (registered packages/session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:981, handler remember.ts:73-92) and the UI/RPC append at packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/sessions.ts:80, whose renderer trigger is `type: 'appendMemory'` at apps/electron/src/renderer/components/app-shell/ChatDisplay.tsx:1557. Readers: readMemoryFile (memory-store.ts:29-33) -> readMemoryFileWithImports (:66-110) -> mergeMemoryContents (:165-183) -> formatMemoryPromptBlock (:139-142) -> loadMemoryPromptBlock (:317-334), and from there the pinned capability context (per packages/shared/AGENTS.md, memory rides `BaseAgent.buildPinnedCapabilityContext()`, composed once per capability generation). PROMPT-CACHE RISK, and it is the real one here: because the fork does not strip frontmatter at load, a `modified:` line that changes on every write becomes a changing line inside the `<memory>` block; mergeMemoryContents dedups by normalised line so the new value is never collapsed away. That is the same shape as the #862 per-minute re-stamp that invalidated Pi's cached system prefix. Either land the load-side frontmatter strip in the same change (memory.md:388) or verify the memory block does not sit in a cached prefix on either backend before shipping. Second-order: readMemoryFile caps at MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200 raw lines (memory-store.ts:8), so frontmatter lines already consume the load budget and one more line moves the cliff by one. The scheduled sweep is unaffected -- cleanupAutoMemoryContent copies unmarked lines byte-identically (memory-cleanup.ts:140-149, 180) and bails on content containing '\r' or above AUTO_MEMORY_CLEANUP_MAX_BYTES (:125). Existing tests that will see the new bytes: packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/remember.test.ts, packages/shared/src/agent/memory/__tests__/memory-store.test.ts, packages/shared/src/agent/memory/__tests__/memory-cleanup.test.ts, packages/shared/src/prompts/__tests__/system.test.ts:90. This CROSSES A PERSISTENCE BOUNDARY -- MEMORY.md is a user-visible, hand-editable on-disk file written atomically at mode 0600 (remember.ts:44-48, memory-store.ts:127-131) and the fix rewrites bytes a human may own -- so it is a risk trigger in this repo. It does NOT cross a wire/schema boundary: no IPC/RPC payload, tool schema (RememberSchema) or session-mirror shape changes. No imported-plugin path reads these files.
userImpact: None observable for any file the app itself created: both writers seed a new MEMORY.md as `# Memory` plus bullets, so no Nessy-generated memory file has frontmatter for the field to live in. It surfaces the moment a user hand-authors a frontmatter header on their memory file -- e.g. a `---\ntitle: ...\n---` block at the top of `~/.nessy-agent/MEMORY.md` or a project MEMORY.md, which is a normal thing to do to a markdown file they were told they may edit freely (memory.md: 'plain markdown you can edit or delete at any time'). From then on every save -- the agent's `remember` tool and the chat UI's remember action alike -- appends a bullet and leaves that header frozen, so neither the user opening the file nor the model reading it back can tell whether a fact is from today or from three months ago. Today the model gets no freshness signal at all: the only date Nessy records, the per-entry `<!-- nessy:auto:DATE -->` marker, is stripped in mergeMemoryContents before the prompt is built (memory-store.ts:173), so it exists solely so the cleanup sweep can tell agent lines from human ones. What would make the gap visible in a test rather than in the wild: any fixture MEMORY.md that starts with `---`.
